author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Kroger lowered its full-year comparable-sales forecast Friday as slower consumer spending weighed on demand, while leaving its annual profit target unchanged. The grocer now expects identical sales excluding fuel to rise 0.2% to 0.8%, down from its previous 1% to 2% range.

Second-quarter identical sales excluding fuel rose 0.2% in the period ended August 15, compared with 3.4% a year earlier and below the 0.9% estimate compiled by LSEG. Adjusted earnings of $1.09 a share were three cents above the estimate. Kroger said cost controls, e-commerce and retail media helped support profitability despite weaker unit growth.

The company also cited two unusual pressures: a cyclospora outbreak reduced quarterly sales by about 35 basis points, and Medicare drug-pricing changes created an estimated 140-basis-point headwind for pharmacy revenue. Kroger kept its profit guidance as management focuses on sourcing, simpler operations, store openings and faster delivery. The revised sales view adds to evidence that middle- and lower-income shoppers are emphasizing essentials and value as inflation continues to strain household budgets.
dek: The grocer kept its profit outlook after a quarterly earnings beat, but lowered its comparable-sales range amid softer demand.
headline: Kroger trims sales forecast as shoppers pull back
